description: The easiest, full-featured wireless router setup for Debian-based devices. Period.

summary.one_liner: RaspAP is a web-based wireless router and access point manager for Raspberry Pi and other Debian-based boards, with a browser UI for hotspot, DHCP, VPN, and ad-blocking settings.
summary.what_it_does: RaspAP turns a Debian-based device with wireless hardware into a configurable Wi-Fi router or access point, managed through a responsive web interface. It offers advanced DHCP settings, WireGuard and OpenVPN client support, and Tailscale and VPN provider CLI integration (VPN provider support is marked beta). It can generate SSL certificates via mkcert for HTTPS, enable DNS-based ad blocking, and configure a routed or bridged AP. The README also covers 802.11ac 5GHz mode on supported hardware, captive portal integration, themes, and multilingual messages via GNU Gettext. A PluginManager lets developers add custom plugins, and a Docker container is offered as an alternative to the installer.
use_cases: turn a Raspberry Pi into a Wi-Fi router
set up a wireless access point with a web UI
route Wi-Fi clients through an OpenVPN or WireGuard tunnel
block ads and trackers on a home network
run a bridged or routed hotspot on an Orange Pi or Armbian board
configure DHCP ranges for a small network
how_to_run: Option 1: flash a pre-built Raspberry Pi OS Lite image with RaspAP (from the latest release page) using Raspberry Pi Imager or balenaEtcher
Option 2: on a clean Raspberry Pi OS install, run sudo apt-get update, sudo apt-get full-upgrade, sudo reboot
Set the WiFi country with sudo raspi-config (Localisation Options)
Run the Quick installer: curl -sL <installer URL> | bash (the URL is missing from the README text provided)
Default login after install: admin / secret; AP SSID RaspAP, password ChangeMe; change these immediately
Docker and manual installation are also documented in the README (linked separately)
notable: Pre-built Raspberry Pi OS Lite images (32- and 64-bit) with RaspAP preinstalled
Quick installer script with command-line switches, including --cert for HTTPS setup
Built-in plugin framework (PluginManager) with a SamplePlugin starter repo
Supports Debian-based distros including Kali Linux, Armbian, and Debian 12/13 (some marked beta)
Bridged AP mode and 802.11ac 5GHz support on listed hardware
caveats: Targets Debian-based devices only; many distros are beta or community-supported, and 'supported' is not guaranteed
802.11ac 5GHz is limited to listed hardware (RPi 3B+, 4, 5 and compatible Orange Pi models)
VPN provider CLI control is a new beta feature
